assessments.reasoning: The nonlocal statement section identifies enclosing function-local scopes, resolves multiple qualifying bindings to the nearest, and specifies SyntaxError on absence of a qualifying binding. Previously bound is the reference’s lexical name-binding language. The statement is a parser directive. The nearest qualifying function scope can be farther out than the immediately enclosing one, and the claim does not imply an already executed outer assignment. Applies to nonlocal in a nested function or class, with the target in an enclosing function scope. The grammar supports more than one declared identifier, with the rule applied per name. The nearest existing function-local binding wins. A module-only binding leaves no qualifying nonlocal scope. Prior use or assignment can separately raise SyntaxError, and type parameters belong to annotation scopes whose names cannot be rebound by nonlocal.

challenge.method: Trace nested scopes with two candidate bindings, with only a farther binding, and with only a module name. Check use before the declaration and the same edition’s type-parameter scope rule.
challenge.results: The nearest existing function-local binding wins. A module-only binding leaves no qualifying nonlocal scope. Prior use or assignment can separately raise SyntaxError, and type parameters belong to annotation scopes whose names cannot be rebound by nonlocal.

limitations: The claim does not describe module globals or CPython's compiler implementation.
The absence of a qualifying binding is a sufficient cause of SyntaxError. Prior use in the declaring block is a separate cause.
The same edition excludes names in annotation scopes from nonlocal rebinding. A valid lexical nonlocal reference does not guarantee an outer value is initialized at the point of a later read.
